## Fixes

- **Codex shows its model and status without hooks.** Codex used to fall under "everything else": it showed no status unless it reported for itself, and its model appeared only when it was launched with `--model`. The reconciler now reads Codex's visible UI the way it reads Copilot's. An active "esc to interrupt" indicator means working, approval and input dialogs mean blocked, and a ready composer means idle. The model comes from Codex's footer, or from the startup banner in older versions, so a `/model` switch appears on the next scan.

  Codex launched with `-m <id>` now also gets its model from the command line. That short alias applies only to Codex, because other programs may use `-m` for something else.

  Detection depends on Codex's terminal layout. A screen it doesn't recognize keeps the last known state, and an explicit `tmux-legion report` still takes precedence. See [Codex detection](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion#codex-detection).

## Install

### Nix flake

```nix
# Pin to a release tag (recommended); drop the ref to track the default branch.
inputs.tmux-legion.url = "github:hawkish/tmux-legion/v0.7.1";
```

### Manual and TPM-style

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion
cd ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion && cargo build --release
echo 'run-shell ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-legion/tmux-legion.tmux' >> ~/.tmux.conf
```

Upgrading needs a tmux config reload, not just a rebuild — see [After upgrading](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion#after-upgrading). The [README](https://github.com/hawkish/tmux-legion#install) covers Claude Code hooks, the agent skill, and the pi extension.
